Note::NlpAccessor::tokens¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::NlpAccessor::tokens(std::int64_t flags = 0) const

Tokenize Each Cell Into Word-Like Units¶

tokens() splits each text cell into word tokens and returns them as a TokenBatch. It sits one step above split_whitespace: instead of “everything between spaces,” it recognizes word shapes and drops the punctuation between them, so "One.\nTwo!" tokenizes to One, Two — no trailing . or !.

What counts as a word¶

The tokenizer is ASCII-oriented. A word is a run of ASCII letters and digits, with a few extensions:

  • _ is part of a word (snake_case is one token).

  • A single - or ' between two alphanumeric characters stays inside the word (state-of-the-art, don't).

  • Trailing + or # after a letter is kept (C++, C#).

  • URLs, email addresses, and common dotted abbreviations are recognized and kept whole rather than shattered on their . and /.

Everything else — spaces, standalone punctuation, and every byte outside ASCII — is a separator. That last point matters: a non-ASCII letter breaks the word around it, so "café2" tokenizes to caf, 2 and "über-cool" to ber-cool. The regex accessor also uses ECMAScript byte-oriented matching; it can define an explicit boundary but does not add Unicode character classes. Normalize or transliterate the text first when an ASCII token vocabulary is acceptable.

flags¶

flags is a bitmask; flags <= 0 (the default) leaves tokens as they appear in the source. Bit 1 << 0 (value 1) case-folds every emitted token (ASCII lowercase) without changing the token boundaries — convenient for building a bag-of-words key in one call instead of chaining lower.

The TokenBatch result¶

Tokens from all cells are concatenated into the rank-1 Note batch.tokens(). The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run: cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). A cell with no word contributes an empty range.

Example 1: Punctuation Is Dropped¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"One.\nTwo!", "price=12.50, paid!"}).nlp().tokens();

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["One", "Two", "price", "12", "50", "paid"]
offsets: [0, 2, 6]

The ., !, =, and , are all separators; 12.50 splits at the ..

Example 2: The Case-Fold Flag¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"Ada LOVELACE", "Grace Hopper"}).nlp().tokens(1);
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["ada", "lovelace", "grace", "hopper"]

Example 3: Without The Flag¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"Ada LOVELACE"}).nlp().tokens();
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["Ada", "LOVELACE"]

Example 4: Per-Cell Runs¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({{"a b", "c d e"}}).nlp().tokens();

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]
offsets: [0, 2, 5]

The 1×2 input flattens row-major: cell 0 → [0, 2), cell 1 → [2, 5).
